scope: Capacity arithmetic for the owned three-party/six-direction relay star at configured continuous payload rates, not measured speech quality or an available-bandwidth estimator. Every media path crosses two hops; two direction FIFOs each cap UDP payload at1024kbit/s. Hop orientation can differ; the sum over both FIFOs is the invariant.

assumptions.excluded: QUIC/TCP/IP/ACK,RTCP,video,files,padding,FEC bitrate variation and other traffic. Shaper charges UDP payload bytes including QUIC, excluding IP/UDP headers.

inference: At20ms/32000payload,modeled audio alone totals2208000bit/s across both hops,exceeding the two FIFO caps2048000bit/s before QUIC/control/video/files. Quiet/good receiver reports cannot by themselves fund that promotion. At60ms/24000 ->40ms/24000,the modeled increment is152000bit/s one-hop-equivalent (50666.667bit/s per source) plus excluded transport/control costs. It must be reserved by reducing actual competing source work or established extra capacity. Do not impose this test-specific rate as a universal group limit.
limits: Configured payload budgets differ from observed VBR/DTX output. Arithmetic does not claim every packet uses the configured payload rate.
An average packet-size model cannot be summed as exact traffic cost across a fragmentation boundary. Use actual size distribution or a conservative packet ceiling for admission/funding.
Arrival rates in100ms bins measure bursts,not link capacity or packet loss. No claim that instrumentation has zero timing effect.
RTP counters used for audio are logical; video fanout attempts and RTCP accepted copies already include peers. Never multiply those latter totals by peer count again.
